clue.text: Journeyed from American island to speak

indicators.note: to speak tells us the island's name is said out loud, giving a word with a different spelling

parts.note: Rhode Island is a US state, named after the island of Rhode

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off from an American island in order to give a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: RHODE, from Rhode Island in the US, is pronounced just like the past tense of ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple past-tense synonym: to have ridden somewhere is to have journeyed there.

clue.text: Give a new interpretation of advice, once excellent

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for advice or counsel
fine means excellent

explanation.surface: Someone reinterprets advice that used to be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the archaic word REDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a fresh meaning or reading is to define it again.

clue.text: Take a chance, as prolific artist

definitions.meaning: to settle something by picking straws or similar
what an artist who sketches a great deal does

explanation.surface: A busy artist gambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: to decide by random picks, and literally to sketch a great deal, as a prolific artist would.

clue.text: Cavalier returns no bow — fret about this

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the misty word is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: a fret is a sea mist rolling in off the coast, as in sea fret

indicators.note: returns means the little word no is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
a bow is a curved structure, an arch

explanation.surface: A dashing horseman turns down a bow and worries about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fret' looks like the verb 'worry', but on Britain's east coast a fret is a sea mist. 'returns' makes ON, and 'about' wraps the mist round it and the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: In the English Civil War the Cavaliers were the supporters of King Charles I, so a Cavalier is a royalist.

clue.text: Ancient, or 17

indicators.note: 17 refers to the answer at 17 down, meaning having lost its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: in heraldry or is the tincture gold, so golden

explanation.surface: A query whether something is ancient, or another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 down's answer, BEHEADED, works as the deletion signal, removing the first letter. 'or' is heraldry's word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is a literary adjective for times long past, as in 'olden days'.

clue.text: City school-teacher puts head down on block

indicators.note: puts head down means the first letter is moved further down the word in this down clue

parts.note: a master is a male schoolteacher
a dam blocks a river

explanation.surface: A teacher rests their head on a block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts head down' moves the M of MASTER down one place to make AMSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, an example of a city.

clue.text: Needled, being stuck in house over holiday, one gets all lit up

definitions.text: Needled, being stuck in house over holiday, one gets all lit up

parts.words: Needled, being stuck in house over holiday, one gets all lit up
parts.note: a cryptic picture of a needle-covered fir brought indoors for the festive season and hung with lights

explanation.surface: Someone irritated at being stuck at home over the holidays gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needled' and 'lit up' suggest annoyance and drunkenness; read literally they describe a fir with needles covered in fairy lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorated fir set up indoors each December has needles and is strung with lights.

clue.text: Old raiders not at first appearing in history book

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: the Vikings were Norse raiders of the early Middle Ages

explanation.surface: Ancient raiders are absent at first from a history text.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as 1 Kings, the Old Testament book recounting the history of the kings of Israel and Judah.
explanation.definitionFit: 1 Kings is one of the historical books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Start to hunt through odds and ends of things for a garment

indicators.note: through means the starting letter of hunt is threaded into the other letters
odds means the odd-numbered letters are taken
ends of means the first and last letters are taken
Start to means only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone begins hunting through a pile of odds and ends for something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds and ends' reads as a stock phrase for clutter, but here it names two separate picks from the one word 'things', and 'through' threads the H between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting legwear item, a garment covering the legs and hips.

clue.text: The hard stuff suited one

definitions.meaning: the hardest natural substance is a gem made of carbon
a playing card of one of the four suits, red and lozenge-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone in a suit drinks strong liquor and it agrees with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the hardest natural mineral, and a card of one of the four suits in a pack.

clue.text: Loveliest daughter was ruined, making false accounts

indicators.note: ruined signals that the letters are wrecked and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A beautiful daughter's ruin gives rise to untrue stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Old wives' tales are superstitious beliefs passed on as truth, so they are untrue stories.

clue.text: Enjoying the waves? One shortly holds evidence of shark

indicators.note: holds means the shortened wave contains the shark's sign within it
shortly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: one of the waves, a surge being a large swelling wave
a fin breaking the surface is the classic sign that a shark is near

explanation.surface: A swimmer enjoying the sea spots a shark's fin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' stands for one of the waves just mentioned, a SURGE; 'shortly' trims it to SURG, which holds FIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding breakers on a board is how a person enjoys the waves, with the question mark flagging the playful slant.

clue.text: From traditional entertainment, fan locked out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A spectator is shut out of a traditional show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'locked out', but it is the anagram signal working on FAN and LOCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Country dancing handed down through generations is a customary form of entertainment.

clue.text: A lot of sense

definitions.meaning: a great deal, as in 'a ... better'
vision, one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A good deal of common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: informally a large amount, as in 'a sight more', and the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: Be unconcerned with what Gable told Leigh he did, frankly

definitions.text: what Gable told Leigh he did, frankly
definitions.meaning: Clark Gable as Rhett Butler says to Vivien Leigh's Scarlett, 'Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn' in Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A film buff recalls the famous parting line from Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: an idiom for not caring at all, and the line Rhett Butler says he does not do.

clue.text: I hit boxer violently in shower

indicators.note: violently signals the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer gets hit hard while in the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' looks like a wash, but it is one who shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows work at a gallery or fair is a person who shows, an exhibitor.

clue.text: There's calculated psychological pressure in chess, for example

definitions.meaning: chess is a contest of thinking, an intellectual pastime

explanation.surface: Chess involves calculated psychological pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a manipulative tactic to unsettle someone, and a game of pure intellect such as chess.

clue.text: Fatally cut Howard's End

definitions.meaning: Catherine Howard, Henry VIII's fifth wife, died on the block in 1542

explanation.surface: A critic savages a film of Howard's End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Howard's End' looks like E. M. Forster's novel, but it is how Catherine Howard died.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: killed by having the head cut off, and the fate of Catherine Howard.

clue.text: State London borough has empty properties to rent

parts.note: Newham is a borough in east London

indicators.note: empty means the word is emptied of its inside letters, leaving only its ends

parts.note: to hire something is to rent it

explanation.surface: A London council owns vacant homes available to let.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only P and S of 'properties'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, in New England, named after the English county of Hampshire.

clue.text: Sees it coming? Not altogether; this could be fun

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone foresees something only partly, and expects it to be fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television genre designed to be funny, so it could well be fun.

clue.text: Mace, a weapon raised — about time I left

indicators.note: about means the turned weapon goes around the shortened word
raised in a down clue means the weapon is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: left means the I is removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing its I

explanation.surface: Someone armed with a mace raises a weapon around the time they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mace' looks like the club, but it is the spice. In a down clue 'raised' reads the weapon upwards as NUG, and 'left' drops I from the time word to go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is the spice made from the lacy covering of the nutmeg seed, so the two are closely linked spices.

clue.text: Into Brazil, say, one following another Northerner

indicators.note: following means this unit comes after the other single letter

parts.note: another one, again the Roman numeral

indicators.note: Into means the numeral goes inside the kind of nut

parts.note: a Brazil is an example of a nut
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller heads into Brazil, one after another, though from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil, say' is the Brazil nut. I goes into NUT for NUIT, which follows 'another' I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous people of Arctic Canada, Greenland and Alaska, so one is a northerner.

clue.text: Man who made report, sounding in drink

indicators.note: sounding tells us a word for drink is spoken aloud to give a surname

parts.note: a beverage is any drink

explanation.surface: Someone files a report while sounding off over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: William Beveridge wrote the 1942 report that laid the foundations of Britain's welfare state.
explanation.definitionFit: The economist William Beveridge authored the famous wartime report on social insurance in Britain.

clue.text: Come to see a bomb's what is needed

parts.note: the V1 flying bomb of WWII, written VI, plus the 's
it means the very thing required, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a bomb is just what's needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit someone is to call on them, going round to see them.

clue.text: Arrived by chance in court

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, meaning arrived
lot means fate or chance, as in casting lots

explanation.surface: Someone turned up in court quite by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the legendary seat of King Arthur, so it names a royal court.

clue.text: Waiter brings meat course, then runs through bill

parts.note: a stew is a meat dish served as a course

indicators.note: runs through bill means the cricket letter is pushed into the advertisement

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an ad
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A waiter serves a meat dish and then hurries through the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like the restaurant check, but it is a poster, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward attends to passengers on a ship or plane, serving food and drink as a waiter does.

clue.text: I say Margaret is not gay, your worship

indicators.note: I say signals the words that follow are to be spoken aloud

parts.note: Mag is a pet form of the name Margaret; is gives IS; straight means heterosexual, not gay

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a court official with a remark about a woman's sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'Mag is straight' runs together into the title of a lay judge.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a magistrate is addressed in court as 'your worship', so the form of address stands for the office.

clue.text: Darling girl shortly has to travel
